title: user-mgmt-service
description: Application metrics of the Spring Boot user_mgmt_service, scraped through the backend PodMonitor in charts/auth-stack: routes (rate, latency, errors, in-flight, bytes), the database hop (HikariCP pool, repository calls), the runtime (JVM, threads, GC, log levels), the image's own health checks - plus the container resources of the same pods.

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: Requests per second served by the API, all endpoints.

panels.title: Error rate (5xx)
panels.description: Share of responses with a 5xx status - the SLO-relevant error rate.

panels.title: Response time (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile of the server-side request duration over 5 minutes.

panels.title: Instances up
panels.description: Backend pods currently answering the PodMonitor scrape on the admin port.

panels.title: Running version
panels.description: Image tag of the scraped pods (app.kubernetes.io/version, copied onto every series by the PodMonitor).

panels.title: Waiting for a DB connection
panels.description: Threads queued for a HikariCP connection right now; anything above 0 for minutes means the pool or the managed database is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Request rate by outcome
panels.description: Micrometer's outcome tag: SUCCESS, REDIRECTION, CLIENT_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR.

panels.title: Response time percentiles
panels.description: Quantiles computed from the http_server_requests histogram.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Server errors (5xx) and client errors (4xx) as a share of all responses. The PrometheusRule alerts on the 5xx series.

panels.title: Request rate by endpoint
panels.description: Per URI template (path variables are collapsed, e.g. /users/{id}); NOT_FOUND, REDIRECTION and UNKNOWN are Micrometer's fallbacks for requests outside the route table.

panels.title: Response time (p95) by endpoint
panels.description: Which endpoint is slow, not just that something is.

panels.title: Requests in flight by endpoint
panels.description: http_server_requests_active: what is being handled right now; a route that keeps climbing is waiting on something (the pool, the database).

panels.title: Bytes by endpoint
panels.description: Request bodies received (in) and response bodies sent (out) per route.

panels.title: Connections and threads
panels.description: Open connections on the request listener (keep-alive included) and Tomcat's request threads; busy threads at the configured maximum means the connector is saturated.

panels.title: Connection pool
panels.description: HikariCP connections per state, summed over the backend pods; pending is what requests are waiting for.

panels.title: Connection timing
panels.description: Average time to obtain a connection from the pool, time a connection is held per use, and time to create a new one against the managed database.

panels.title: Repository calls by method
panels.description: Spring Data repository invocations per second (UserRepository: save, findByEmail, findById, ...), the database work behind the routes.

panels.title: Repository call latency (p95) by method
panels.description: Where the database time goes: the p95 per repository method; ERROR state calls appear in the legend when they happen.

panels.title: JVM memory
panels.description: Used memory per area of the GraalVM native-image runtime (heap = eden + survivor + old generation).

panels.title: Threads, GC and CPU
panels.description: Live JVM threads, the share of CPU the garbage collector takes, and the process CPU share as the runtime sees it.

panels.title: Log events by level
panels.description: logback_events_total per level: an error rate in the logs next to the error rate on the wire.

panels.title: Health checks (1 = ok)
panels.description: health_check_up per check from the admin port: spring-context (the application context is up) and database (the managed PostgreSQL answers). A failing check makes /readyz answer 503 and takes the pod out of rotation.

panels.title: Health check duration
panels.description: How long each check took in its last cycle (the timeout bound is HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT); a rising line is a dependency getting slower before it fails.

panels.title: backend pods - CPU
panels.description: cAdvisor usage of the containers against the limit from the environment overlay.

panels.title: backend pods - memory
panels.description: Working set of the containers against the limit; this is what the OOM killer looks at.

panels.title: backend replicas
panels.description: Ready replicas against what the HorizontalPodAutoscaler wants (Aufgabe 6).
